Alternative theories of gravity that go beyond the Riemannian framework have been proposed to explore quantum gravity and to relate string theories.  We analyze these theories within the context of double field theory, validating their consistency and providing a direct field theory path to explore their characteristics.  Additionally, we develop new actions that deviate from these alternatives by adjusting the exponential terms in the action principles.  These revised actions are still consistent with the T-duality symmetries of string theory.  We conclude by examining the toplevel vacua of double field theory to explore the possibility of recovering the original alternative gravity theories.  However, a fully non-perturbative recovery of these theories remains a challenge.  We discuss the potential advantages of using double field theory as a midpoint to explore quantum gravity.  Finally, we outline avenues for further research in alternative theories of gravity within the context of string theory.  This research pathway could provide insights into the broad range of theories that relate to string theory, including those that propose significant modifications to the gravitational force at the event horizon of black holes.  A full investigation remains a subject for future work.  We outline the relevant steps to explore the alternative theories, beginning with a direct field theory path involving four-derivative actions described in this article.  However, the exploration of other aspects of these theories, such as their holographic duals and quantum properties, remains a topic for further research.  An example of progress along this line can be found in the pre-publication titled "Entanglement entropy of alternative gravity, the effective action of a 2D black hole and the Unruh Unruh effect in the Alternative gravity for any dimension".  The direct field path may help to uncover the quantum gravity properties of these theories. We can explore further the quantum gravity properties of this theory and use it to understand quantum Hall systems in relation to string theory. To meet growing demands for "smart home" WiFi services, delivering high-speed video streaming, secure surveillance, and control over IoT devices, it is essential to ensure optimal home network performance. However, this is often hindered by the limited capabilities of existing WiFi standards. In response, a new method has been proposed to improve home WiFi performance by identifying and removing unnecessary access point transmissions. This is achieved through a resource usage monitoring system, which leverages the IEEE 802.11k/v standards to identify optimal AP placement and merge overlapping cells under a single AP. By achieving these goals, this method can dynamically balance AP loads, reduce interference, and increase overall WiFi performance. A performance evaluation was conducted on a realistic home network setup and the results show load merging capabilities up to 80% and overall throughput improvements of 25-40%. This method not only enhances home WiFi performance but also reduces power consumption of APs and prolongs battery life of extender batteries, which is of particular importance in large-scale home networks. A demonstration device was designed and developed to showcase the load performance monitoring and load merging capabilities. This device was successfully tested in a real-world home network setup with multiple APs and IoT devices. This method has been found to be effective and efficient and provides a practical solution for optimizing home WiFi performance and power consumption. A performance evaluation was conducted and the results show that the method can adapt to real-time network conditions and effectively balance AP loads. This method can be easily integrated with existing home networks and does not require modification to the underlying WiFi standards. A performance evaluation was conducted and the results show that the method can be effective in real-world home network settings with a high level of activity from IoT devices.
